title: Only Slim and Bubbles influenced him; Bill Bailey's creation
summary: Green says only J. D. and John Bubbles influenced him, with Raymond Winfield and Walter Beatty, preferring original work, and describes Bill Bailey's invention of the one-foot cramp.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

blocks.x: And then later we will get back into all the dancers that you met through your career and their particular styles. And also how they influenced you and the change of their styles through the years.
Yes. Well, there were only two that inspired me, and that was J. D. -- which I called "Slim" Chuckles, and John Bubbles of Buck and Bubbles, you see.
All the other dancers you didn't find that --

No -- I -- I enjoyed them immensely, but I'm saying they weren't an influence on me -- well, there was two more, there was Raymond Winfield and Walter Beaty, you know. I had my moments, too, you know. I was -- I would rather do an original work than try to do something -- an impression of another tap dancer, see. It's like introducing a new degree to tap dancing. Eventually you can create -- you can introduce a creation, see. Like eventually be a Bill Bailey -- after Terry Wilson discovered him he went away for about -- about four weeks on his own somewhere, and he came back with a new creation of tap dancing which is -- had the one-foot cramp and all that in it. See, because tap dancing then was almost -- most of them was trying to learn how to do the John Bubbles which is cramps, you know, and the kick cramps and the tap

turn, you see. And he had ways of doing -- performing that was infectious to other people that especially was in the same art -- tap dancing, you know. Well, the fraternity used to call them desserts -- like the end of the meal you have the sweets, you know, and that's the way they used to appear, you know. It was like a refreshment, you know.
